title: Tiered signal prioritization and adaptive rollback windows for Optimize evals
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Context: As Optimize expands to run continuous regression checks across heterogeneous prompt sets and customer cohorts, we need a decision framework that (1) prioritizes which signals should force immediate rollback versus staged mitigations, and (2) uses adaptive monitoring windows to avoid flip-flopping when metric noise is high. Current playbooks conflate quality, safety and perf signals and rely on fixed time windows; this has led to false positives during low-traffic cohorts and slow responses for high-severity safety regressions.

Goals:
- Define a tiered signal taxonomy (Critical / High / Medium / Low) mapping to automated actions (Immediate rollback / Canary stop & investigation / Increased sampling & alerting / Observe).
- Specify quantitative thresholds, minimum sample sizes, and statistical rules for A/B decisions and canary stoppage that work across small and large promptset cohorts.
- Design adaptive rollback windows: short windows for high-confidence, high-severity signals, expandable windows for noisy, low-signal cohorts.
- Produce acceptance criteria and runbook snippets for engineering and SRE to implement automated enforcement in the Optimize pipeline.

Scope (in):
- Eval signals produced by Optimize (quality metrics, safety/hallucination rate, latency p95, token cost per prompt).
- A/B and canary gating logic tied to rollout pipelines and the Console rollout UI.
- Automated enforcement hooks (stop rollouts, pause rollouts, increase sampling) driven by the composite decision matrix.

Out of scope (for this ticket):
- Deep model-specific offline evaluation tooling (separate PRD).
- Full integration with external customer SLAs (handled in a follow-up enterprise contract workstream).

Signal taxonomy and example thresholds (proposal):
- Critical (safety / data integrity): hallucination rate increase >= 0.5 percentage points AND relative increase >= 25% relative to baseline OR any SAFETY_THRESHOLD_VIOLATION flagged by safety classifier. Action: Immediate automated rollback + incident page. Rationale: safety must preempt other considerations.
- High (quality): absolute drop in primary quality metric (e.g., promptset pass@1 / correctness score) >= 1.5 percentage points AND statistically significant (two-sided test, p < 0.01). Action: Pause rollout, route traffic to control, open investigation, run extended canary.
- Medium (performance/cost regressions): latency p95 increase >= 20% OR token cost per prompt increase >= 15% with sample N >= 1000. Action: Throttle rollout (reduce weight), increase batching suggestions, notify owners.
- Low (minor variability): small, likely-noise shifts (quality delta between 0.3–1.5 pp) without statistical significance. Action: Monitor with increased sample and no automated stoppage.

Statistical decision rules and minimum sample sizes: 
- Minimum sample per cohort for any automated action: 2000 requests per variant for quality/safety signals. For small cohorts (<2000) use Bayesian posterior monitoring and require higher evidence factor (e.g., Bayes factor > 10) before automated actions.
- A/B significance: two-sided chi-squared (for binary pass metrics) or t-test for continuous metrics with Bonferroni correction when multiple metrics are evaluated simultaneously. Default alpha = 0.01 for high-priority signals.
- Sequential testing: for long-running rollouts we will adopt an SPRT-inspired sequential monitor with pre-specified Type I/II error tolerances to allow earlier detection while controlling false alarm rates. Engineering spike required to select tuning constants.

Adaptive rollback windows:
- Start window: 1 hour for high-traffic cohorts, 6 hours for medium cohorts, 24 hours for low-traffic cohorts.
- Expand-contract heuristic: compute per-metric coefficient of variation (CoV) over the window. If CoV > 0.25, extend window by factor 2 up to 72h. If CoV < 0.10 and sample size above minimum, shrink window toward the start window.
- Example: a small enterprise promptset with N=800/day shows noisy quality signal: monitoring starts at 24h window, CoV=0.4 -> expand to 48h. If after 48h signal remains inconsistent, escalate to manual triage rather than automated rollback.

Composite decision matrix: each decision point combines (1) signal tier, (2) statistical evidence, (3) cohort size and stability (CoV), and (4) business priority (customer impact). We will encode weights for these axes (suggested initial weights in runbook) and translate resulting score to actions: 0-0.4 Observe, 0.4-0.7 Increased sampling & throttle, 0.7-0.9 Pause rollout & investigate, >0.9 Automatic rollback.

Runbook snippets and integration notes:
- Safety immediate rollback: webhook from Optimize monitor to rollout controller -> rollback route -> post-incident ticket auto-populate with last successful model version and first bad request samples.
- Canary stop: automatically reduce traffic to 0% for variant after pause condition, enable 100% control routing, trigger extended canary with doubled sampling for 48–72h.
- Notification: route high/critical alerts to on-call SRE + model owner; medium alerts to owner + ticket in backlog.

Success metrics for this initiative:
- Reduce false-positive automatic rollbacks by 40% on low-traffic cohorts within 3 months of rollout.
- Reduce mean time to rollback for critical safety regressions to < 15 minutes.
- Maintain pass rate for legitimate quality regressions (true positives) >= 95% (i.e., avoid missing real degradations).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Exact statistical tests and alpha thresholds to standardize across all metrics (engineering spike required).
- Implementation of Bayesian fallback for small cohorts vs. strict sample-size gating.
- UI affordances in Console to display adaptive window status and composite score.

Next steps / proposed plan:
1) PM finalize thresholds and decision matrix (this ticket) — two-week window for feedback.
2) Eng spike (ENG-21450) to validate SPRT tuning and Bayesian monitors on historical optimize runs.
3) SRE design of automated rollback webhooks and incident creation (ENG-27891).
4) Console changes to show window/CoV and composite score (DES-14320).
5) Small-scale dogfood rollout to internal workloads, measure false positives/negatives, iterate.

Owners: PM (Maya Thompson), Eng lead for spike (Luis Alvarez), SRE (Priya Nanduri), Design owner (Ethan Cole).
acceptance_criteria: A decision matrix document exists that maps signal tiers to automated actions and is approved by Eng, SRE, and PM.
Quantitative thresholds for Critical/High/Medium/Low signals are agreed and written here; acceptance requires sign-off from Safety and Platform owners.
Minimum sample size and statistical rules are specified; an engineering spike ticket (ENG-21450) is created and linked.
Adaptive window heuristics (start/expand/contract rules) are defined with example calculations and verification plan.
Runbook snippets for immediate rollback and canary stop are drafted and validated via tabletop exercise with SRE.
Console mockups for displaying composite score and window status exist and have design review feedback attached (DES-14320).
Dogfood rollout completed on at least 3 internal promptsets, with false-positive rollback rate measured and <= 40% compared to baseline.
